name: card-rail
title: Card Rail
description: Card carousel animation: cards flicked sideways on a tilted 3D plane. A rail of cards flicked sideways across a tilted plane. The cards do not crawl past on a loop — they are flicked: the rail leaves at speed, decelerates for well over a second and comes to rest about a card further along, the way a carousel behaves under a thumb rather than under a timer. The plane is not flat to the camera either. Measured on a recording's card edges, the horizontal scale grows 0.000825 per pixel of height about the frame's own centre line, so the foot of a card is a fifth wider than its head while horizontals stay horizontal and the type stays upright — which is why a row of plain rectangles reads as a surface receding into the frame rather than as a filmstrip.
docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/scenes/card-rail?ref=cli — images, titles, notes and tags are parallel lists split by `|` (not by comma: a data: URL has one of its own), one entry per card, and the rail repeats them rather than running out. Leave the text fields blank and the picture becomes the whole card, which is how a card designed elsewhere is handed in as one image. heading holds the top of the frame; from is the frame the flick starts on and may be negative to open mid-flight; offset is where the rail sits before it moves. backdrop takes two colour stops or one picture. Pass mode="dark" if you are rendering onto a dark frame — these default to shadcn's light palette. — 73 Pro components too — charts, launch scenes, device shots: https://snapcn.dev/docs/pricing?ref=cli-docs
